newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu ends weaker, activity picks up.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu ends weaker, activity picks up.

text.p: Romania's leu ended Monday weaker with dealers' quotes ranging from 8,750/900 to 9,100/200 to the dollar, slightly down from the morning levels of 8,650/8,950.

Dealers said trading on the interbank market, which has been affected by a chronic shortage of hard currency in recent months, had revived following moves by the central bank to restore local dealer licences to 24 banks last week. They act as market makers along with the previous four dealers.
"One can see signs of revival on the market. But let's not get too excited about it," a dealer said.
Latest central bank (BNR) data showed interbank trading amounted to $7.75 million last Friday, compared with a daily average of some $609,000 in January.
Dealers said a relative shortage of lei on the market in recent days might slow the leu's downward trend.
"I reckon the leu might stabilise for a while near the 10,000 (to the dollar) level and eventually even strengthen a bit," one said.

Dealers said they were still waiting for the BNR's possible new moves after last week's announcement that it would no longer compute the leu's reference rate, which was a guidance rate used for statistical accounting purposes.
The BNR set the leu's reference leu for Monday -- the last such operation -- at 7,744 lei to the dollar.
Leu-dollar prices at licenced money changing bureaux ranged from 7,900/8,400 to 8,100/8,600.
